@graph.name: Portfolio & Case Studies — Thomas Cherickal
@graph.description: Selected technical content case studies across Generative AI Content and Quantum Computing Technology — the brief, the approach, and what shipped.

item.headline: How to Run Your Own Local LLM — 2026 Edition — Version 1
item.description: A deep technical survey and operational guide evaluating the top 10 open-weight frontier LLMs running on a Quad Nvidia DGX Spark cluster (4x GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchips, 512GB unified AI memory, ~4 PFLOPS FP4 compute), pairing benchmark performance with a ~$36K total deployment blueprint including a Lenovo ThinkStation PX Command Centre, multi-model co-hosting, and power/thermal specifications.
item.keywords: local LLM deployment, Quad Nvidia DGX Spark, GB10 Grace Blackwell, DeepSeek V3.2, Qwen3.5, Lenovo ThinkStation PX, MoE quantization, vLLM, Command Centre

item.headline: Google Gemini vs Anthropic Claude vs OpenAI ChatGPT vs xAI Grok: The Ultimate Comparison
item.description: The definitive 2026 comparative evaluation of the four AI titans—Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI ChatGPT, and xAI Grok—analyzing technical strengths, ecosystem moats, and corporate strategies to declare category winners across reasoning, writing, coding, enterprise trust, real-time data, and creative tasks, with Claude taking the #1 overall crown.
item.keywords: frontier AI benchmarks, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Code, Google Gemini 3 Deep Think, GPT-5.4 Computer Use, xAI Grok 4/5, Constitutional AI, enterprise AI strategy

item.headline: The Hidden Geometry of Generative AI: How Manifold Theory Explains the Mysteries Nobody Explained to You
item.description: A masterclass in geometric deep learning explaining seven major unsolved riddles of generative AI—from diffusion score matching and GAN mode collapse to latent space soap bubbles and Flow Matching—through the single unifying lens of differential manifold theory, presented twice (once in plain English, once for the math-curious) with zero equations.
item.keywords: manifold hypothesis, differential geometry, score-based diffusion, Flow Matching, geodesics, optimal transport, Wasserstein distance, slerp, latent space geometry

item.headline: Nobody Knows How LLMs Work – Unless You Look at Them as Non-Linear Dynamical Systems
item.description: A physics-grounded technical treatise reframing large language models as high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems governed by autoregressive feedback loops—explaining Chinchilla scaling (the 20-to-1 rule), emergent capabilities as physical phase transitions, grokking as a bifurcation into generalizing Fourier circuits, and why deep networks operate at the 'Edge of Chaos' (lambda ≈ 0).
item.keywords: nonlinear dynamical systems, transformer architecture, chaos theory, grokking, Lyapunov exponents, phase transitions, Chinchilla scaling, residual stream ODE

item.headline: The OpenClaw Saga: How the Last Two Weeks Changed the Agentic AI World Forever
item.description: A technical chronicle and architectural post-mortem of the February 2026 OpenClaw revolution—analyzing its autonomous local-first execution, the rapid spawning of community forks (ClawRouter, Moltbook, PicoClaw, SecureClaw, ClawBands, IronClaw), the critical CVE-2026-25253 WebSocket RCE vulnerability, and why local quantized SLMs/LLMs are displacing vendor-locked cloud agents.
item.keywords: agentic AI, OpenClaw ecosystem, CVE-2026-25253, ClawRouter, PicoClaw, SecureClaw, ClawBands, IronClaw, edge agent runtimes, local tool calling

item.headline: Hermes Agent vs OpenClaw: Which AI Agent Framework Wins in 2026?
item.description: A comprehensive architectural shootout contrasting Nous Research's Hermes Agent (agent-first, compounding learning loop) against OpenClaw (gateway-first, multi-channel routing)—evaluating why Hermes provides the first secure, practical self-improving agent framework through three-tier persistent memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md and SQLite FTS5 SessionDB), the SKILL.md self-evolution engine, and Tinker-Atropos GRPO reinforcement learning pipelines.
item.keywords: agent frameworks, Hermes Agent, Nous Research, OpenClaw, persistent memory, SQLite FTS5, self-improving skills, GRPO reinforcement learning, sandbox isolation

item.headline: Comparing Quantum Programming Frameworks: IBM Qiskit, Microsoft Q#, and Quantinuum’s New Stack
item.description: An in-depth comparative architectural evaluation of three leading quantum programming ecosystems—IBM Qiskit, Microsoft Q#, and Quantinuum's three-tier stack (Guppy, Selene, Helios)—evaluating developer ergonomics, abstraction layers, and compilation pipelines with practical code examples implementing the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) for molecular simulation (H2 ground state energy).
item.keywords: IBM Qiskit, Microsoft Q#, Quantinuum Stack, Guppy, Selene, Helios, VQE, H2 molecular simulation, Azure Quantum

item.headline: Quantum Computing Fundamentals Part I: 10 Easy Pieces
item.description: A foundational curriculum guiding classical software engineers through 10 essential quantum principles—from qubits, superposition, and the Bloch sphere to Bell state entanglement, measurement collapse, the no-cloning theorem, quantum teleportation, and decoherence—illustrated with detailed explanations and self-contained, executable Qiskit Python circuits.
item.keywords: quantum computing fundamentals, IBM Qiskit, Bloch sphere, Bell state entanglement, quantum teleportation, no-cloning theorem, decoherence, Python

item.headline: Quantum Computing Fundamentals Part II: 10 Not-So Easy Pieces
item.description: The concluding masterclass in the Quantum Fundamentals series covering 10 advanced quantum algorithms and industry techniques—including Shor's factoring algorithm, QFT, QPE, Hamiltonian simulation, quantum annealing, 3-qubit error correction, Grover's search, and VQE—with complete source code, circuit diagrams, and execution instructions.
item.keywords: Shor's algorithm, Quantum Fourier Transform, QPE, quantum error correction, Grover's algorithm, Hamiltonian simulation, VQE, IBM Qiskit, Python

item.headline: How Quantum Computers Threaten Bitcoin and the Entire Internet: Simply Explained
item.description: A clear, accessible breakdown of how quantum computing acts as a ticking time bomb against modern public-key cryptography—explaining how Shor's algorithm breaks RSA and Bitcoin's ECC (secp256k1), the urgent 'Store Now, Decrypt Later' (SNDL) crisis, logical qubit timelines (2035–2040), and the global race to transition to NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography standards.
item.keywords: post-quantum cryptography, NIST PQC standards, Shor's algorithm, CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium, SPHINCS+, Bitcoin ECDSA vulnerability, Store Now Decrypt Later

item.headline: OpenFang: The Game-Changing Open Source Agent OS That Replaces OpenClaw
item.description: A deep systems-engineering and security analysis of OpenFang—a 137,000-line Rust agent operating system (14 crates, single 32MB binary, 40MB idle RAM, 180ms cold start) designed to replace fragile chatbot wrappers like OpenClaw with 16 defense-in-depth security layers, 7 autonomous Hands, and kernel-enforced permission gates.
item.keywords: OpenFang, Rust Agent OS, OpenClaw replacement, WASM sandbox security, autonomous Hands, CVE-2026-25253, Agent-to-Agent protocol, MCP server

item.headline: Inside Jev: How Decision Models Trade Text Generation for Typed, Calibrated Answers
item.description: An architectural deep dive into TypeSafe AI's Jev—the first 'System One' decision model that trades token-by-token text generation for typed, parallel judgments with calibrated probabilities, cutting inference latency to 70–500ms and reducing agent decision costs by up to 98.7% ($0.042/M input tokens, free outputs).
item.keywords: decision models, TypeSafe AI Jev, System One AI, calibrated probabilities, RLCD, fast inference, agentic routing, Jevons paradox

item.headline: Gemini Spark versus Hermes Agent versus OpenClaw: Who Wins and Why?
item.description: A definitive 3-way architectural shootout contrasting Google's managed 24/7 cloud agent (Gemini Spark), Nous Research's open-source self-improving agent (Hermes Agent), and the viral gateway pioneer (OpenClaw)—evaluating security posture, persistent memory architectures, runtime autonomy, and enterprise viability.
item.keywords: Gemini Spark, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, autonomous agents shootout, persistent cross-session memory, self-improving loops, Antigravity harness, enterprise AI security

item.headline: The AI Olympics: Which $20 AI Subscription Plan Wins in 2026?
item.description: An exhaustive multi-vendor showdown evaluating nine $20/month AI subscription plans across 10 empirical categories—benchmarking ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro, Google AI Pro, SuperGrok, Kimi Moderato, Meta AI (Muse Spark), MiniMax Plus, Copilot Pro, and Perplexity Pro across coding, writing, research, and multimodal generation.
